BUNKERGAME — FULL BUNKER GENERATION MASTER PROMPT
PHASE: BUNKER FIRST / WORLD MAP LATER

Build a complete new production-quality bunker for BunkerGame.

This is a full bunker generation and integration task.

The immediate objective is to create the complete bunker as one coherent,
playable, visually consistent survival-horror facility.

DO NOT build or redesign the surrounding world map yet.

The surrounding exterior world, terrain, forest, roads, landmarks,
resource zones, and larger map composition will be a separate phase after
the bunker has passed final acceptance.

==================================================
0. PRIMARY GOAL
==================================================

Generate, compose, integrate, and verify a complete underground bunker
for BunkerGame.

The bunker must feel like one intentionally designed facility rather than
a collection of disconnected generated rooms.

Target presentation:

- high-quality Roblox survival-horror environment
- abandoned / deteriorating underground military-civil-defense facility
- believable functional architecture
- oppressive and creepy atmosphere
- strong environmental storytelling
- visually rich without excessive clutter
- readable navigation
- gameplay-ready spaces
- coherent materials, dimensions, lighting language, and prop families
- modular enough to support later expansion
- optimized for Roblox

The result must be suitable to become the central landmark and primary
interior environment of the future BunkerGame map.

==================================================
1. SAFETY / BACKUP BOUNDARY
==================================================

Before ANY project, Studio, terrain, or filesystem mutation:

1. Inspect the current BunkerGame state.
2. Create a fresh verified recoverable backup.
3. Record the backup path and verification evidence.
4. Identify gameplay-critical systems, anchors, remotes, scripts,
   interactions, spawn dependencies, farming dependencies, and any other
   systems that must survive bunker replacement/integration.
5. Do not perform destructive replacement until the backup and dependency
   inventory are verified.

Never use workspace.Terrain:Clear().

Do not perform broad destructive terrain operations.

Any terrain operation must first identify exact occupied regions and then
use targeted modification only.

==================================================
2. SOURCE OF TRUTH
==================================================

Respect the current BunkerGame source-of-truth architecture.

Determine the current relationship between:

- filesystem
- Rojo
- Roblox Studio
- generated/imported assets
- Asset Library
- runtime state

Permanent implementation must be persisted through the project's
canonical filesystem/Rojo workflow.

Do not leave permanent Studio-only edits.

Do not silently overwrite newer authoritative project state.

==================================================
3. EXISTING SYSTEM PRESERVATION
==================================================

Before generation, inspect the existing game and classify relevant content
as:

REUSE
MIGRATE
REPLACE
RETIRE
PROTECTED

Preserve functional gameplay systems unless replacement is explicitly
required for the bunker architecture.

Pay special attention to:

- player spawn
- interaction systems
- inventory
- harvesting/resources
- farming
- processors
- bunker interactions
- UI dependencies
- progression dependencies
- doors
- power/electrical systems
- navigation assumptions
- enemy/navigation dependencies
- scripts referencing existing bunker objects or paths

Do not break gameplay merely to obtain a cleaner visual result.

==================================================
4. ASSET LIBRARY FIRST
==================================================

Before generating any reusable asset:

Search the approved BunkerGame Asset Library.

Reuse approved assets and asset families whenever they satisfy the
required visual/function role.

Known reusable bunker-oriented families should be considered where
appropriate, including existing production-ready industrial/military
assets such as:

- valves
- electrical junction boxes
- ventilation grilles
- rusty pipes
- military storage/ammo crates

Do not regenerate an asset merely because generation is available.

When a new reusable asset is genuinely required:

1. search the Asset Library for the closest approved family
2. use the closest approved asset/family as visual reference when useful
3. generate the new variation through the approved generation workflow
4. perform technical QA
5. perform visual QA
6. register the approved result in the Asset Library
7. persist its provenance and implementation metadata

Rejected/test/temporary assets must not enter the Asset Library.

==================================================
5. GENERATIVE WORKFLOW
==================================================

Use the established BunkerGame orchestration model where available.

Desired responsibility model:

MUSE
- overall art direction
- bunker visual language
- composition review
- visual consistency review
- final visual approval

QWEN
- reasoning
- reference analysis
- generation/reference selection
- architectural and visual support

MIMO
- execution orchestration
- coordinates tool use

ROBLOX ASSISTANT
- Roblox-native generation
- creative asset/environment composition
- image-to-mesh / generation workflows where appropriate

BLOXFORGE
- engineering
- integration
- filesystem/Rojo persistence
- technical corrections
- collision/pivot/anchoring validation
- performance checks
- runtime QA
- evidence collection

Do not claim that any of these agents/tools participated unless they were
actually invoked.

Record orchestration evidence.

==================================================
6. REFERENCE-DRIVEN GENERATION
==================================================

Do not rely on vague text-only generation when a strong visual reference
would materially improve quality.

Reference priority:

1. approved user reference
2. approved BunkerGame Asset Library reference
3. purpose-made generated reference
4. suitable online reference
5. text-only generation when reference imagery adds little value

Maintain a coherent visual language across all bunker rooms.

Do not independently generate every room with unrelated references.

Establish the bunker-wide art direction first.

==================================================
7. BUNKER ARCHITECTURE
==================================================

Design the bunker as a believable connected facility.

The exact layout should be determined from gameplay needs, existing
dependencies, circulation requirements, and visual composition rather
than blindly preserving obsolete geometry.

The facility should include an appropriate set of spaces such as:

- bunker entrance / exterior transition
- blast-door sequence
- airlock / decontamination transition where appropriate
- main circulation corridor
- command/control area
- power/generator room
- workshop / maintenance room
- storage
- sleeping/living quarters
- utility/service spaces
- farming/growing area where required by existing gameplay
- processing area where required
- ventilation/service infrastructure
- secondary corridors
- locked/restricted areas
- believable maintenance access
- environmental-storytelling pockets

Add other rooms only when they strengthen gameplay or facility logic.

Do not create rooms simply to increase bunker size.

==================================================
8. LAYOUT QUALITY
==================================================

The bunker must have:

- understandable primary circulation
- useful secondary circulation where appropriate
- no accidental dead-end navigation traps
- believable room adjacency
- consistent floor elevations
- usable door clearances
- sufficient player traversal width
- camera-safe geometry
- no portal obstruction
- no structural pieces blocking intended entrances
- readable landmarks
- meaningful spatial variation
- strong room silhouettes
- controlled sightlines
- gameplay-relevant chokepoints
- intentional safe/unsafe spatial rhythm

Perform explicit traversal QA before visual polish is considered complete.

==================================================
9. STRUCTURAL KIT
==================================================

Create or reuse a coherent bunker structural kit.

The kit may include:

- floors
- walls
- ceilings
- bulkheads
- columns
- beams
- door frames
- blast doors
- corridor modules
- wall recesses
- ceiling service channels
- ventilation infrastructure
- drainage elements
- pipe supports
- cable routes
- maintenance panels
- grilles
- access hatches
- structural damage variants

Avoid obvious repetitive copy-paste appearance.

Variation must remain within the same architectural language.

==================================================
10. MATERIAL LANGUAGE
==================================================

Use a controlled material palette.

Possible families:

- aged reinforced concrete
- painted military steel
- galvanized/oxidized metal
- rust
- worn industrial paint
- dirty tile where functionally appropriate
- rubber
- aged electrical materials
- damp surfaces
- grime
- localized water staining

Damage and dirt must follow plausible causes.

Examples:

- leaks below pipe/service routes
- rust around exposed metal and drainage
- water staining beneath damaged ceiling infrastructure
- wear around doors and high-traffic areas
- grime around machinery
- cleaner protected surfaces behind removed equipment

Avoid random noise applied uniformly to every surface.

==================================================
11. INDUSTRIAL DETAILING
==================================================

Build believable infrastructure throughout the facility:

- electrical runs
- junction boxes
- conduits
- pipes
- valves
- ventilation
- drainage
- machinery
- service panels
- brackets/supports
- emergency equipment
- storage systems
- maintenance props

Infrastructure should appear connected and purposeful.

Do not scatter industrial props randomly.

==================================================
12. ROOM IDENTITY
==================================================

Every major room must have a distinct functional and visual identity while
remaining part of the same bunker.

A player should be able to recognize major spaces from:

- silhouette
- layout
- equipment
- lighting
- material balance
- environmental storytelling

without relying entirely on UI labels.

==================================================
13. ENVIRONMENTAL STORYTELLING
==================================================

Communicate that the bunker had a real history before the player's arrival.

Use restrained storytelling through:

- abandoned work areas
- interrupted maintenance
- emergency procedures
- damaged infrastructure
- storage organization
- personal traces
- failed repairs
- signs of resource scarcity
- evidence of deterioration
- inaccessible or partially damaged areas

Do not turn every room into a staged story scene.

Prefer environmental implication over exposition.

==================================================
14. LIGHTING
==================================================

Create a deliberate bunker lighting hierarchy.

Use practical fixtures and believable sources.

Possible states include:

- functioning utility lights
- failing fluorescent fixtures
- emergency lighting
- localized darkness
- machinery indicators
- occasional damaged/dead fixtures

Lighting must support gameplay readability.

Darkness should create tension without making navigation unnecessarily
frustrating.

Avoid uniform brightness.

Avoid excessive colored horror lighting.

==================================================
15. AUDIO / VFX
==================================================

Where supported by the current project architecture, prepare the bunker
for restrained atmospheric audio/VFX such as:

- ventilation hum
- electrical buzz
- occasional failing fixture
- pipe/drip ambience
- machinery loops
- distant structural sounds
- localized steam/dust/water effects

Do not overload the environment with constant effects.

Audio/VFX must be spatially and functionally justified.

==================================================
16. GAMEPLAY INTEGRATION
==================================================

The bunker is not a static showcase.

Integrate existing gameplay-critical systems into the new architecture.

Verify:

- spawn behavior
- interactions
- farming
- processing
- inventory-related stations
- doors
- upgrade/inspection stations where applicable
- navigation
- player camera
- collision
- enemy interaction assumptions
- runtime scripts
- UI/gameplay bindings

Do not consider the bunker complete if it looks good but breaks the
existing playable loop.

==================================================
17. PERFORMANCE
==================================================

Keep the bunker suitable for Roblox runtime.

Review:

- part counts
- mesh complexity
- material usage
- texture usage
- lighting cost
- transparency
- collision complexity
- unnecessary hidden geometry
- repeated assets
- streaming implications
- effects
- scripts/connections

Prefer reusable modular assets over needless unique geometry.

Optimization must not destroy the intended visual quality.

==================================================
18. VISUAL QA
==================================================

Perform visual QA after major composition stages.

Review at minimum:

- entrance
- primary corridor
- every major room
- important room-to-room transitions
- farming/gameplay area
- strongest hero views
- weakest views
- lighting consistency
- material consistency
- prop density
- scale
- repetition
- collision-visible artifacts
- obvious generated-asset defects

Do not approve the bunker based only on code, hierarchy, or object counts.

Visual evidence is mandatory.

==================================================
19. TECHNICAL QA
==================================================

Verify:

- no unintended scripts lost
- no broken references
- no missing gameplay anchors
- no invalid asset IDs
- no unanchored static architecture unless intentional
- no accidental collision blockers
- no inaccessible required spaces
- no portal obstruction
- no duplicate critical systems
- no source/live drift left unexplained
- Rojo build passes
- project validation passes
- runtime QA passes

==================================================
20. PLAYTEST QA
==================================================

Perform an integrated playtest.

Test the bunker as a player, not merely as a scene.

Walk the complete intended circulation route.

Test:

- spawn
- traversal
- doors
- interactions
- farming-related interactions
- processing
- critical stations
- camera
- collisions
- room transitions
- lighting readability
- gameplay loop continuity

Any Play session used for QA must be stopped afterward and Studio must be
verified back in Edit mode.

==================================================
21. ITERATION
==================================================

Do not stop after first generation.

Use this loop:

GENERATE
→ INTEGRATE
→ TECHNICAL QA
→ VISUAL QA
→ PLAYTEST
→ IDENTIFY DEFECTS
→ FIX
→ REVERIFY

Continue until the bunker meets the completion gates below.

Do not hide defects behind completion markers.

==================================================
22. WORLD-MAP BOUNDARY
==================================================

DO NOT build the surrounding full map during this task.

Only create the minimum exterior transition necessary to make the bunker
entrance understandable and testable.

Do not yet build:

- full terrain
- forest
- roads
- large exterior POIs
- resource distribution
- world progression layout
- complete exterior lighting composition
- complete exterior ambience

Those belong to the next master phase:

BUNKERGAME — FULL WORLD MAP GENERATION.

The completed bunker must provide a stable anchor from which that map can
later be designed.

==================================================

Do not report completion until all applicable gates pass:

24. ORCHESTRATION TRACE
==================================================

==================================================

milestones.objective: Execute master-prompt sections 12-15 exactly as specified.
requirements:
12. ROOM IDENTITY

Every major room must have a distinct functional and visual identity while
remaining part of the same bunker.

A player should be able to recognize major spaces from:

- silhouette
- layout
- equipment
- lighting
- material balance
- environmental storytelling

without relying entirely on UI labels.

13. ENVIRONMENTAL STORYTELLING

Communicate that the bunker had a real history before the player's arrival.

Use restrained storytelling through:

- abandoned work areas
- interrupted maintenance
- emergency procedures
- damaged infrastructure
- storage organization
- personal traces
- failed repairs
- signs of resource scarcity
- evidence of deterioration
- inaccessible or partially damaged areas

Do not turn every room into a staged story scene.

Prefer environmental implication over exposition.

14. LIGHTING

Create a deliberate bunker lighting hierarchy.

Use practical fixtures and believable sources.

Possible states include:

- functioning utility lights
- failing fluorescent fixtures
- emergency lighting
- localized darkness
- machinery indicators
- occasional damaged/dead fixtures

Lighting must support gameplay readability.

Darkness should create tension without making navigation unnecessarily
frustrating.

Avoid uniform brightness.

Avoid excessive colored horror lighting.

15. AUDIO / VFX

Where supported by the current project architecture, prepare the bunker
for restrained atmospheric audio/VFX such as:

- ventilation hum
- electrical buzz
- occasional failing fixture
- pipe/drip ambience
- machinery loops
- distant structural sounds
- localized steam/dust/water effects

Do not overload the environment with constant effects.

Audio/VFX must be spatially and functionally justified.

milestones.title: GAMEPLAY INTEGRATION → TECHNICAL QA
milestones.objective: Execute master-prompt sections 16-19 exactly as specified.
requirements:
16. GAMEPLAY INTEGRATION

The bunker is not a static showcase.

Integrate existing gameplay-critical systems into the new architecture.

Verify:

- spawn behavior
- interactions
- farming
- processing
- inventory-related stations
- doors
- upgrade/inspection stations where applicable
- navigation
- player camera
- collision
- enemy interaction assumptions
- runtime scripts
- UI/gameplay bindings

Do not consider the bunker complete if it looks good but breaks the
existing playable loop.

17. PERFORMANCE

Keep the bunker suitable for Roblox runtime.

Review:

- part counts
- mesh complexity
- material usage
- texture usage
- lighting cost
- transparency
- collision complexity
- unnecessary hidden geometry
- repeated assets
- streaming implications
- effects
- scripts/connections

Prefer reusable modular assets over needless unique geometry.

Optimization must not destroy the intended visual quality.

18. VISUAL QA

Perform visual QA after major composition stages.

Review at minimum:

- entrance
- primary corridor
- every major room
- important room-to-room transitions
- farming/gameplay area
- strongest hero views
- weakest views
- lighting consistency
- material consistency
- prop density
- scale
- repetition
- collision-visible artifacts
- obvious generated-asset defects

Do not approve the bunker based only on code, hierarchy, or object counts.

Visual evidence is mandatory.

19. TECHNICAL QA

Verify:

- no unintended scripts lost
- no broken references
- no missing gameplay anchors
- no invalid asset IDs
- no unanchored static architecture unless intentional
- no accidental collision blockers
- no inaccessible required spaces
- no portal obstruction
- no duplicate critical systems
- no source/live drift left unexplained
- Rojo build passes
- project validation passes
- runtime QA passes

milestones.title: PLAYTEST QA → WORLD-MAP BOUNDARY
milestones.objective: Execute master-prompt sections 20-22 exactly as specified.
requirements:
20. PLAYTEST QA

Perform an integrated playtest.

Test the bunker as a player, not merely as a scene.

Walk the complete intended circulation route.

Test:

- spawn
- traversal
- doors
- interactions
- farming-related interactions
- processing
- critical stations
- camera
- collisions
- room transitions
- lighting readability
- gameplay loop continuity

Any Play session used for QA must be stopped afterward and Studio must be
verified back in Edit mode.

21. ITERATION

Do not stop after first generation.

Use this loop:

GENERATE
→ INTEGRATE
→ TECHNICAL QA
→ VISUAL QA
→ PLAYTEST
→ IDENTIFY DEFECTS
→ FIX
→ REVERIFY

Continue until the bunker meets the completion gates below.

Do not hide defects behind completion markers.

22. WORLD-MAP BOUNDARY

DO NOT build the surrounding full map during this task.

Only create the minimum exterior transition necessary to make the bunker
entrance understandable and testable.

Do not yet build:

- full terrain
- forest
- roads
- large exterior POIs
- resource distribution
- world progression layout
- complete exterior lighting composition
- complete exterior ambience

Those belong to the next master phase:

BUNKERGAME — FULL WORLD MAP GENERATION.

The completed bunker must provide a stable anchor from which that map can
later be designed.
